standard_prerequisites.name: The notion of an (A, n, c)-module, and the closed subschemes Y_c of the affine blowup algebra used to measure scheme-theoretic support
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on a bit of uniformity, where the counted statement occurs
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the hypothesis on M and the conclusion about where the kernel is supported.

standard_prerequisites.name: The derived-functor description of Tor over a quotient ring and the effect of multiplying by an element of a power of the ideal
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at source lines 5116-5120
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the annihilation of Tor by a power of the ideal into the scheme-theoretic support statement.

core_obligations: Reduce to affine opens: the proof restricts the given short exact sequence to an affine open and rewrites its terms as tensored modules over the quotient by a power of the ideal (proof lines 5102-5110)

Identify the kernel with a Tor module: over the affine chart the kernel of the pullback is computed by the first Tor of M against the quotient algebra, which is the step where the exactness defect is localized (proof lines 5110-5116)

Annihilation: multiplication by an element of the c-th power of the ideal on M factors through a finite free module over the quotient by the n-th power, which shows that the Tor module is annihilated by that power (proof lines 5116-5120)
Conclusion: the kernel is scheme theoretically supported on the closed subscheme cut out by the c-th power, which is the statement (proof line 5120)
proof_roadmap: 在仿射开覆盖 Spec(B) 上把给定短正合序列与模的张量积比较，识别出 kernel 由 Tor_1^{A/I^n}(M, B/I^nB) 给出。
由 (A,n,c)-模的定义，乘 I^c 的元素通过某个有限自由 A/I^n-模分解，故该 Tor 被 I^c 杀死，即 kernel 的概型支撑落在 Y_c 上。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement computes the scheme-theoretic support of the kernel of the pullback of an almost exact sequence of modules (author lemma at source lines 5094-5100, label lemma-almost-exactness): if the outer terms are annihilated by a power of the ideal and the last term is an (A, n, c)-module, that kernel is supported on the closed subscheme Y_c. The proof (source lines 5102-5121) localizes to affine opens, identifies the kernel with a Tor module of M against the quotient algebra (proof lines 5102-5116), and then uses the defining property of an (A, n, c)-module — that multiplication by an element of the c-th power factors through a finite free module over the quotient — to show the Tor module is annihilated by that power (proof lines 5116-5120). The identification with Tor is the step with content. H2.
